front_blocks.md: Define **globalisation**.

back_blocks.md: **Globalisation** is where the world has become more **interconnected** through the processes of **economics, culture, politics, trade and tourism**.

cards.front_md: Define **globalisation**.
cards.back_md: **Globalisation** is where the world has become more **interconnected** through the processes of **economics, culture, politics, trade and tourism**.

front_blocks.md: What **four significant developments** have driven the flows behind globalisation?

back_blocks.md: The appearance of large **transnational corporations (TNCs)**; the growth of **regional economics and trading blocs**; the development of **modern transport networks**; and **advances in IT and communications**, particularly the WWW and the internet.

cards.front_md: What **four significant developments** have driven the flows behind globalisation?
cards.back_md: The appearance of large **transnational corporations (TNCs)**; the growth of **regional economics and trading blocs**; the development of **modern transport networks**; and **advances in IT and communications**, particularly the WWW and the internet.

front_blocks.md: What is meant by the **'shrinking world'**?

back_blocks.md: The idea that improvements in **communication and transport** have made global connections **faster, deeper and longer**, so distant places feel closer together — a key feature of globalisation.

cards.front_md: What is meant by the **'shrinking world'**?
cards.back_md: The idea that improvements in **communication and transport** have made global connections **faster, deeper and longer**, so distant places feel closer together — a key feature of globalisation.

front_blocks.md: What are the **three ways** global connections have changed under globalisation?

back_blocks.md: **Faster** (speeds for talking, travel and money exchange); **deeper** (connecting lives with faraway places); and **longer** (connecting links between places further apart).

cards.front_md: What are the **three ways** global connections have changed under globalisation?
cards.back_md: **Faster** (speeds for talking, travel and money exchange); **deeper** (connecting lives with faraway places); and **longer** (connecting links between places further apart).

front_blocks.md: What are **global cities**?

back_blocks.md: Cities that have developed as the **focus of the world economy**, a key feature of globalisation as political borders become less important and countries more interdependent.

cards.front_md: What are **global cities**?

front_blocks.md: As of **2024**, roughly what proportion of the world's population has internet access?

back_blocks.md: More than **60%** of the world's population has access to the internet.

cards.front_md: As of **2024**, roughly what proportion of the world's population has internet access?

front_blocks.md: How can globalisation **damage cultural diversity**?

back_blocks.md: Some see it as a threat to local cultures because **Western practices often replace traditional ones**, which can damage cultural diversity.

cards.front_md: How can globalisation **damage cultural diversity**?

front_blocks.md: Which two institutions were set up to encourage economic growth and cooperation in the connected world economy?

back_blocks.md: The **International Monetary Fund (IMF)** and the **World Bank**.

cards.front_md: Which two institutions were set up to encourage economic growth and cooperation in the connected world economy?

front_blocks.md: Give **one environmental impact** of globalisation linked to **technology**.

back_blocks.md: **E-waste** contains toxic materials that can leach into soil and water as devices become outdated and are improperly discarded. (Also: pollution from manufacturing, and satellites' carbon footprint and night-sky pollution.)

cards.front_md: Give **one environmental impact** of globalisation linked to **technology**.

front_blocks.md: How does globalisation's growing **transport network** harm the environment?

back_blocks.md: As economies grow, transport networks need **more energy**, increasing **carbon emissions** — shipping and haulage emit **60%** of world emissions.

cards.front_md: How does globalisation's growing **transport network** harm the environment?

back_blocks.md: Infrastructure like **satellites** and fibre optic cables have further improved global communication, enhancing growth and quality of life worldwide.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Globalisation is a completely new phenomenon that did not exist before modern times.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Globalisation is **nothing new** — trade between people, businesses and countries has always existed; modern transport and communications have simply made it almost **instantaneous**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Today, more than half of the world's total economic output comes from goods traded across foreign borders.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
More than **half** of the world's total economic output comes from goods that are **exported and imported** across foreign borders.

front_blocks.md: Define a **transnational corporation (TNC)**.

back_blocks.md: A large organisation that **manufactures and trades goods in two or more countries**, operating in foreign countries **without a centralised management system** and with **no** particular country as its corporate home.

cards.front_md: Define a **transnational corporation (TNC)**.
cards.back_md: A large organisation that **manufactures and trades goods in two or more countries**, operating in foreign countries **without a centralised management system** and with **no** particular country as its corporate home.

front_blocks.md: What is the key difference between a **TNC** and an **MNC**?

back_blocks.md: An **MNC** has a **home country** that makes decisions and passes them around its global companies, whereas a **TNC** operates **independently** without a centralised management system.

cards.front_md: What is the key difference between a **TNC** and an **MNC**?
cards.back_md: An **MNC** has a **home country** that makes decisions and passes them around its global companies, whereas a **TNC** operates **independently** without a centralised management system.

front_blocks.md: Why do TNCs locate **R&D** in HICs but **factories** in LICs?

back_blocks.md: **R&D** goes in **HICs** for access to **highly skilled labour and funding**; **factories, call centres or service hubs** go in **LICs** where **labour is cheap** and there are usually **reduced legal restrictions**.

cards.front_md: Why do TNCs locate **R&D** in HICs but **factories** in LICs?
cards.back_md: **R&D** goes in **HICs** for access to **highly skilled labour and funding**; **factories, call centres or service hubs** go in **LICs** where **labour is cheap** and there are usually **reduced legal restrictions**.

front_blocks.md: How does **McDonald's** show that TNCs adapt to **local markets**?

back_blocks.md: It changes its menu per country — e.g. **macarons and bleu cheese burgers** in France, **boerie and hash brown stacks** in South Africa, and the **Maharaja Mac** in India.

cards.front_md: How does **McDonald's** show that TNCs adapt to **local markets**?

front_blocks.md: How do TNCs use **supply chains** to drive the global economy?

back_blocks.md: They often **source raw materials** from one country, **manufacture** in another, and **sell** their products in multiple other countries, acting as the **main investors** in the global economy.

cards.front_md: How do TNCs use **supply chains** to drive the global economy?
cards.back_md: They often **source raw materials** from one country, **manufacture** in another, and **sell** their products in multiple other countries, acting as the **main investors** in the global economy.

front_blocks.md: How has the movement of TNC manufacturing benefited countries like **China, India and Brazil**?

back_blocks.md: It has helped transform them from **low-income countries (LICs)** into **middle-income countries (MICs)**, directly benefiting their populations.

cards.front_md: How has the movement of TNC manufacturing benefited countries like **China, India and Brazil**?
cards.back_md: It has helped transform them from **low-income countries (LICs)** into **middle-income countries (MICs)**, directly benefiting their populations.

front_blocks.md: Define **Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR)**.

back_blocks.md: Voluntary actions by TNCs to **improve society** — e.g. donating to charity, cutting carbon footprints, paying fair wages — which can boost **brand reputation, employee engagement and customer loyalty**.

cards.front_md: Define **Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR)**.
cards.back_md: Voluntary actions by TNCs to **improve society** — e.g. donating to charity, cutting carbon footprints, paying fair wages — which can boost **brand reputation, employee engagement and customer loyalty**.

front_blocks.md: Give **two positive social impacts** of TNCs on host countries.

back_blocks.md: They bring **skills, opportunities, money and technology**, **create jobs** (so people can buy more and pay more tax), and increase **social mobility** through education, apprenticeships and progression.

cards.front_md: Give **two positive social impacts** of TNCs on host countries.
cards.back_md: They bring **skills, opportunities, money and technology**, **create jobs** (so people can buy more and pay more tax), and increase **social mobility** through education, apprenticeships and progression.

front_blocks.md: Give **two negative economic impacts** of TNCs on host countries.

back_blocks.md: **Small local businesses cannot compete**; a **labour drain** as skilled workers migrate; **dependence** on a single TNC; and **profits 'leaking' out** of the host country as bonuses and dividends to shareholders.

cards.front_md: Give **two negative economic impacts** of TNCs on host countries.
cards.back_md: **Small local businesses cannot compete**; a **labour drain** as skilled workers migrate; **dependence** on a single TNC; and **profits 'leaking' out** of the host country as bonuses and dividends to shareholders.

front_blocks.md: Give **one negative environmental impact** of TNCs.

back_blocks.md: **Lax environmental laws** in developing countries can cause severe air, water and soil pollution; TNCs also **deplete natural resources** and contribute heavily to **greenhouse gas emissions**.

cards.front_md: Give **one negative environmental impact** of TNCs.
cards.back_md: **Lax environmental laws** in developing countries can cause severe air, water and soil pollution; TNCs also **deplete natural resources** and contribute heavily to **greenhouse gas emissions**.
